title: Write Your First Factory
description: Author a factory of your own: one workstation, one worker, one goal.
openingSummary: A factory is a graph of workstations and workers described in configuration. The smallest useful one has a single workstation that hands a goal to a single agent worker.

whatItIs.title: What It Is
whatItIs.body: Writing a factory means declaring what work exists, who does it, and how work moves between them. Everything else — retries, review, fan-out — is added to that skeleton later.

whenToUse.title: When To Use
whenToUse.body: Use this once a packaged factory has done something close to what you want, but not close enough. Start from the smallest graph that runs, then grow it.

stepsOrWorkflow.title: Steps Or Workflow
stepsOrWorkflow.body: Scaffold a factory, replace the starter workstation with your own, point it at a worker, then run it.

commonPitfalls.title: Common Pitfalls
commonPitfalls.body: Do not start by describing the whole workflow. A factory that does not run teaches you nothing; a factory that runs badly teaches you exactly what to fix next.
